<br />


The objective of this five-day training course, co-organized by the
[FRB-CESAB](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/about-the-foundation/le-cesab/), the 
[UMS PatriNat](https://www.patrinat.fr/) and the [Cirad HortSys](https://ur-hortsys.cirad.fr/)
is to train young researchers on the methods and techniques of meta-analyses 
and systematic reviews/maps applied to the field of biodiversity.

**N.B.** This training course is **in French**, but slides are available in English.



<br />



## Program

### Monday

|       | Session                                           | Trainer | Material                                                                        |
| ----: | :------------------------------------------------ | :-----: | :-------: |
| 9:00  | Welcome and icebreaker                            | All     |                                                                                 |
| 9:30  | Introduction to evidence synthesis                | DB      | [slides](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/01-introduction.html) |
| 10:30 | Stakeholder engagement in systematic reviews      | JL      | [slides](courses/engaging-stakeholder-2026.pdf)                                 |
| 11:15 | Planning a systematic review: the protocol        | JL      | [slides](courses/planning-a-systematic-review-2026.pdf)                         |
| 14:00 | Literature search: databases and search equations | SC      | [slides](courses/literature-search-2026.pdf)                                    |
| 15:00 | Corpus organisation and reference management      | NC      | [slides](https://literaturesynthesis.github.io/corpus-management)               |
| 15:45 | Screening: title, abstract and full text          | SC      | [slides](courses/screening-2026.pdf)                                                 |
| 16:30 | Retrieving full-texts                             | NC      | [slides](https://literaturesynthesis.github.io/retrieving-fulltext)             |
| 17:00 | Reporting standards (ROSES)                       | JL      | [slides](courses/reporting-standards-2026.pdf)                                  |



### Tuesday

|       | Session                                                | Trainer | Material  |
| ----: | :----------------------------------------------------- | :-----: | :-------: |
| 9:00  | Corpus visualisation approaches                        | JL      | [slides](courses/corpus-visualisation-2026.pdf)                                    |
| 9:20  | Workshop: from hypotheses to a systematic map          | JL/DV   | [slides](courses/from-hypothesis-to-codebook-2026.pdf)                             |
| 10:30 | Codebook construction and testing                      | JL/DV   | [slides](courses/codebook-construction-2026.pdf)                                   |
| 14:00 | R practical: mapping the evidence **^(a)^**            | DV/DB   | [slides](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/02-td-evidence-map.html) |
| 14:45 | Automated techniques: introduction to machine learning | DV      | [slides](courses/introduction-to-ai-2026.pdf)                                      |
| 16:15 | Applying the RAISE guidelines                          | DV      | [slides](courses/introduction-to-ai-2026.pdf)                                      |

**^(a)^** Material for practice available [here](02-td-evidence-map_TD.html)



### Wednesday

|       | Session                                                         | Trainer | Material |
| ----: | :---------------------------------------------------------------| :-----: | :------: |
| 9:00  | Effect sizes **^(b)^**                                          | DB      | [slides](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/03-effect-sizes.html) |
| 10:00 | Critical appraisal and study validity                           | JL      | [slides](courses/critical-appraisal-2026.pdf)                                   |
| 11:15 | Quantitative data extraction: methods and tools **^(c)^**       | JL      | [slides](courses/quantitative-data-extraction-2026.pdf)                         |
| 14:00 | Fixed, random and multilevel models **^(d)^**                   | DB      | [slides](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/04-models.html)       |
| 15:00 | Publication bias and sensitivity **^(e)^**                      | DB      | [slides](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/05-bias.html)         |
| 16:15 | Why does the effect vary? Moderators and missing data **^(f)^** | DB      | [slides](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/06-advanced.html)     |
| 17:00 | Group work: discussion and constitution of groups               | All     | |

**^(b)^** Cheatsheet on effect sizes formula available [here](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/03-effect-sizes_formula_sheet.pdf)<br>
**^(c)^** Sample papers available [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fCz5eYuqeYyvGC4zFngAK1AXMJ2C2Aly)<br>
**^(d)^** Material for practice available [here](https://dbeillouin.github.io/cours_Meta_analyses/04-models_TD.html)<br>

## Prerequisites

Please follow this [tutorial](https://frbcesab.github.io/rsetup/) to install your working environment before attending the training course. Note: for this course only **R** and **RStudio Desktop** are required.
